title: dynamic batching: add sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization heuristics
author: Marcus R. Lee
release_notes: Introduce sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization heuristics for dynamic batching. Improves throughput and reduces wasted tokens for mixed-length workloads. Backwards-compatible runtime flags exposed for tuning.
description:
Motivation: Mixed-sequence-length workloads (chat + embeddings + short prompts) cause dynamic batching to pad many sequences to the longest length in a batch, increasing token cost and reducing throughput. This PR implements a light-weight bucketing heuristic that groups requests by sequence-length buckets and schedules bucket fills to minimize padding while keeping latency SLOs.

What this PR does:
- Adds a sequence-length bucketing layer on top of the existing continuous batcher. Buckets are defined by configurable boundaries (e.g. [0,64,128,256,512]).
- Implements a padding-minimization scheduler that prefers filling same-bucket requests and only merges across adjacent buckets when the max_wait threshold is reached.
- Adds a token-cap per-batch heuristic (max_batch_tokens) to prevent pathological large batches when many short requests arrive.
- Integrates bucket-aware KV-cache pinning so KV caches are reused for same-model same-seqlen batches while allowing cache sharing when safe.
- Exposes runtime flags and per-tenant config: seqlen_buckets, max_batch_tokens, bucket_merge_delay_ms, bucket_priority_policy.
- Adds metrics: batching.bucket_fill_rate, batching.padded_token_ratio, batching.avg_bucket_latency, batching.bucket_sizes (histogram).

Design notes:
- Buckets are kept coarse to avoid fragmentation; by default we use logarithmic boundaries. The scheduler is greedy but bounded: it will wait up to bucket_merge_delay_ms for same-bucket arrivals, then merge adjacent buckets if needed to respect latency SLOs. This keeps median latency stable while reducing padding.
- KV cache integration: caches are keyed by (model, variant, bucket_id) to maximize reuse. We added a small eviction policy to avoid cache explosion for many buckets.
- We chose a token-cap rather than batch-size cap because token count better correlates with GPU work when sequences vary widely.

Checklist:
- [x] Core bucketing and scheduler implementation (runtime C++).
- [x] KV-cache integration and eviction policy.
- [x] Unit tests for bucket assignment and merge behavior.
- [x] Perf microbench harness and results.
- [x] Config/flags and runtime toggles.
- [x] Docs and changelog snippet.

Performance summary (see benchmarks section below): typical mixed-length customer workloads show a 9% net throughput improvement and a 23% reduction in padded tokens. Median latency remains within 1ms of baseline; p95 improves ~6% due to fewer oversized batches.

Related: ENG-5123 (dynamic batching improvements), ENG-5239 (kv-cache evictions), related PRs: pr-35622-dynamic-batching-seqlen-bucketing-padding.json.

Notes for reviewers: the changes touch the hottest path in the serving runtime; pay attention to lock contention in dynamic_batcher and correctness of KV-cache keys across rollouts. I included a conservative default (buckets off) so this can be staged behind a feature flag.

benchmarks_summary: Mixed-length synthetic workload (50% short <64, 30% mid 64-256, 20% long >256) on 2xA100: +8.9% throughput
Padded token ratio: baseline 31% -> new 24% (23% reduction)
Cost estimate: ~6% CPU/GPU token-cost reduction for these workloads (model dependent)
